cat > /tmp/pr_body.md <<'EOF'
## What

The second Fort Dearborn's blockhouse gets the cupola its own pictures draw, and loses the
invented chimney that was standing in its place. **This is a bounded partial increment of
T-2388** — the ticket's all-buildings, all-pictures acceptance is NOT met and the ticket is
released OPEN with the remaining differences recorded.

Panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet of 1893, captioned "Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835", draws
this blockhouse with a small square body at the centre of its four-sided cap, under a little
four-sided cap of its own, and draws no stack anywhere on that roof. The two Wau-Bun
reproductions of the 1831 view (`kinzie_1857_chicago_1831_panorama`) draw the same body. That is
what is now built.

| | |
|---|---|
| before | the invented brick stack at the apex |
| after | the pictured cupola, seated into all four roof planes |

`docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/` holds both, rendered through `photo_match.mjs` from
**one identical camera** with nothing changed between them but the blockhouse's own bytes
(`4b49f0db…` → `96d9fb80…`), beside the panel itself.

## Why, and what is and is not claimed

* **The cupola's OCCURRENCE is inferred** from the two identified pictures. Every dimension —
  the 1.8 m side, the 2.1 m body, the 0.22 m cap eave, the 36° cap pitch, the 0.12 m seat, the
  plain boarded sides with no louvres and no finial — is **reconstructed**, lives in the
  archetype rather than the record, and is admitted in `docs/LIBERTIES.md`
  § `L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388`. A tier-5 retrospective chromolithograph supplies
  form, never a metric, and its caption is not proof the feature stood on 1 July 1835.
* **`chimneys: 0` is a choice about what to DEPICT, not a finding about heating.**
  `_chimneys` stands its single stack at exactly the centre of the plan — the cupola's place —
  so the two could not both be built and one of them is pictured. The record says in as many
  words that this is not a claim of no heating, no flue, or no later secondary projection, and
  the stack has not been quietly moved somewhere else. The 1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print (filed
  misleadingly as `chicago_fort_dearborn_river_mouth_1830.jpg`) depicts about 1836–1849 and does
  show a louvred cap and an ambiguous projection beside it; that later detail is left
  unresolved, not backdated.
* **The join is real.** A box set down at the apex floats clear of the covering at its own
  corners, because the pyramid falls away in every direction — a strip of sky, and somewhere to
  hide a stack. The body's foot is carried 0.12 m below the lowest the main roof reaches
  anywhere under its footprint, so it comes up through all four planes. The main roof is the
  same four planes `_hip_roof` has always laid.

## How

* `fort_structure_params.py`: a keyword-only, **default-off** `cupola` field (added to
  `CONSUMED`, read by `from_phase`), its five reconstructed dimensions as named module
  constants, and validation that accepts **only the combination that is built** — a
  `blockhouse`, a `pyramid` roof, and no separately generated centre stack — with every
  dimension bounded and checked finite. Existing records and callers keep exactly their previous
  semantics; nothing is turned on globally.
* `fort_structure.py`: a local `_cupola` helper, called from `_building` only when the record
  asks. **Not** the lighthouse's `lantern` (only `_tower` consumes that, so setting it on a
  blockhouse would add nothing at all), not routed through the tower builder, no shared geometry
  changed. `_hip_roof`'s own overhang is now a named constant so `_cupola` reads it instead of
  copying the literal.
* `data/structures/fort_dearborn_blockhouse.json`: `form.cupola` (inferred, with its sources and
  reasoning), `form.chimneys` 1 → 0 with the full admission, and the `roof_type` note corrected —
  it used to end "no cupola is built here".
* The record keeps the `fort_structure(kind=blockhouse)` / `log_1816` phase, the surveyed seat
  and 8° rotation, the inferred 14.52 × 9.80 m footprint **and its ±25 % ambiguity**, the 5.2 m
  reconstructed walls, two storeys, the 0.45 m jetty, loopholes, doors, main pyramid at 30° and
  every palette.

## The 25-master family

Changing the producer stales every `fort_structure` asset, so **all 25 current masters** — the
already accepted 1832 lighthouse and the Lake House construction shell included — were genuinely
rebuilt on pinned **Ubuntu 26.04 / Blender 4.5.3** in two bounded native batches before the first
source commit. All 25 `inputs_sha256` in `assets/manifest.json` are the regenerated ones.
**Exactly one master's bytes moved** — `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb`,
134,632 → 133,092 — and its WEB derivative was re-encoded; the other 24 came back
byte-identical and keep their genuinely bound existing derivatives. No foreign registry row was
touched, and no other job's source, claims or branches were gone near.

## The picture on the card

`kurz_allison_1893` is cited by the record, which is what puts it on the Images tab through
`compile_pictures.py`. `data/structure_grades.json` carries an explicit **pictured ruling**
saying why panel 5 is a reasonable whole picture of this named building, so the sidecar grade
derives `attested` from the rule — not hand-typed, and **not** taken as a camera-fit shortcut:
the only camera on this panel is the T-3040 compound diagnostic, whose eye reached its imposed
100 m bound, and the ruling says so.

## Verification

* `tools/check.sh --part 1/4`, `2/4`, `3/4`, `4/4` — **all four PASS**, every one a bounded
  foreground run (part 1 re-run after `compile_source_use.py` rebuilt its backlinks). No gate
  step reported a missing module.
* `tools/compile_liberties.py`, `tools/compile_scene.py --all`, `tools/compile_source_use.py`,
  `tools/changelog-entries.mjs --check`, `tools/publish.sh` — all clean.
* Before/after compound comparison through `photo_match.mjs`, same camera, both committed.
* Smoke: the parts `tools/smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` names for this diff, at **1280×800 and
  390×780**, reported in a comment below.

## What is NOT claimed

The view's verdict is **`differs`** and `T-2388` is **released OPEN**. Still open on this
building's own picture: the camera is an unfitted 100 m diagnostic and is marked
`diagnostic_only`; the galleried range's identity, the facade openings, the other roof forms and
chimney counts, and the compound's whole composition are unresolved; and the other dated
pictures the ticket lists have not been read against the model at all. Only the roof assembly is
marked `fixed`. No new photo ticket, no split, no `done --pr`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
